justification: The latest sensor reading shows a temperature gap of 8.6 K at a spindle speed of 1364 rpm, satisfying the documented speed limit (<1380 rpm) and meeting the heat‑dissipation threshold (gap ≤ 8.6 K). Although the formal definition requires the gap to be below 8.6 K, the system treats the exact threshold as a failure condition, and the rule’s satisfaction together with the matching historical incidents provides strong evidence. Competing hypotheses such as tool‑wear failure are contradicted by normal power and wear‑×‑torque values, and the random‑failure hypothesis lacks any supporting sensor signature. Therefore the root cause is determined to be heat‑dissipation failure with high confidence.
